target: with-me-ness (perceptual and conceptual)
note: Gaze-based measure of teacher-student co-attention, split into perceptual (following the teacher's deictic gestures, via entry time/first-fixation-duration/revisits) and conceptual (following the teacher's verbal discourse, normalized by slide duration) components (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.7-10).

target: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
note: Mapped (this entry's own extension) onto the paper's 'motivation' construct (deep vs. surface, SPQ) paired with with-me-ness as an operationalized attention/co-attention measure; the paper itself never uses 'engagement' or 'flow' (P/anticipatory-application).

target: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
note: Mapped (this entry's own extension) onto the AOI-miss scanpath variable, defined as a participant who did not fixate an AOI at all during its on-screen period, glossed as 'completely ignoring some parts of the slides'; no attention-failure/meta-awareness literature is cited by the source itself (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.6, with P/anticipatory-application for the construct mapping).

target: monotony / meaninglessness
note: Thin/tangential: the Introduction's complaint that click-stream analytics fail to capture 'passive video watching' gestures at a low-engagement viewing mode adjacent to monotonous consumption, but is never developed as a construct or measured (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.1, with P/anticipatory-application for the construct mapping).

target: gaze variance / fixation dispersion
note: SMI RED 250 eye-tracker (250 Hz); content coverage (heat-map attention-point area) and scanpath variables (AOI misses, AOI backtracks); N=40; content coverage fully mediates motivation->learning, scanpath variables partially mediate it, and good-performer/high-motivation students show fewer misses, more backtracks, more coverage (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.4-9, 11, 13, 15-16).

target: self-report / survey scale
note: Study Process Questionnaire (Biggs, Kember & Leung 2001), 10-item 5-point Likert (5 deep/5 surface); N=40; mean motivation 2.10 (SD=1.20); used as predictor in every mediation model (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.4, 10-11).

target: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
note: Post-video, instructor-validated 10-question multiple-choice quiz; N=40; mean learning score 6.9/10 (SD=1.6); used as outcome in every mediation model and as one of two ML prediction targets (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.4, 10-11).

target: ML classification
note: VGG-19 pretrained-CNN heat-map feature extraction (1,000->100 features/slide) + LASSO feature selection (10-fold CV) + five benchmarked regression algorithms (Gaussian Process, SVM, Random Forest, GAM); N=40 (32 train/8 test, 5-fold CV); best result 5.04% NRMSE (learning) / 9.04% NRMSE (motivation), both Gaussian Process polynomial kernel; these are continuous-score regressions, not discrete classifiers, though ML classification is this cluster's nearest controlled-vocabulary label (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.11-12, 14-15, 17).

target: Sharma, K., Jermann, P., & Dillenbourg, P. (2014) -- 'With-me-ness': A gaze-measure for students' attention in MOOCs
note: The 2014 paper defined with-me-ness and correlated it with learning gains; this paper explicitly extends that analysis to include student motivation as an independent variable, learning as the dependent variable, and gaze behavior as the mediating variable (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.9-10).

target: Biggs, J., Kember, D., & Leung, D.Y. (2001) -- Study Process Questionnaire (R-SPQ-2F)
note: Source of the deep/surface motivation instrument used as the predictor variable throughout the mediation analyses (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.4, 10).

target: Baron, R.M., & Kenny, D.A. (1986)
note: Mediation-analysis three-condition test procedure applied to every gaze variable against motivation (predictor) and learning (outcome) (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.10).

target: Just, M.A., & Carpenter, P.A. (1980) -- A theory of reading: From eye fixations to comprehension
note: Eye-mind hypothesis grounding the paper's basic warrant for treating gaze as an attention proxy; also quoted directly ('there is no single mode of reading') to contextualize the paper's own reading-time finding (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.3-4, 15-16).

target: Simonyan, K., & Zisserman, A. (2014) -- Very deep convolutional networks (VGG-19)
note: Pretrained CNN architecture used to extract 1,000 features per gaze heat-map image in the prediction pipeline (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.11-12).

target: Tibshirani, R. (1996) -- Regression shrinkage and selection via the lasso
note: LASSO feature-selection method (10-fold cross-validation for the shrinkage parameter) applied after VGG-19 feature extraction (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.11-12).

target: Dillenbourg, P., & Traum, D. (2006) -- Sharing solutions: grounding in multimodal collaborative problem solving
note: Grounding theory used to interpret conceptual with-me-ness as a gaze-measure of a student's effort to sustain common ground with the teacher (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.16).

target: Jermann, P., & Nussli, M.A. (2012)
note: Cited supporting finding that better-performing pairs show more recurrent gaze patterns during moments of deictic reference, corroborating the perceptual with-me-ness result (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.16).

target: Kizilcec, R.F., Papadopoulos, K., & Sritanyaratana, L. (2014)
note: Video-instruction design study (showing the instructor's face on screen) cited both as prior eye-tracking-in-education work and as a design-implication touchpoint for gaze-informed MOOC video design (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.3-4, 17-18).

target: Prieto, L.P., Sharma, K., Dillenbourg, P., & Jesus, M. (2016)
note: Teaching-analytics/orchestration-load eye-tracking study cited as prior evidence that eye-tracking data is an important source of information in educational settings (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.3).

target: Pelanek, R. (2015)
note: Source of the Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (NRMSE) metric used to evaluate every prediction result (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.12).

target: Sharma, K., Caballero, D., Verma, H., Jermann, P., & Dillenbourg, P. (2015a, 2015b)
note: Self-citations to collaborative/joint-attention eye-tracking studies in MOOC and pair-programming contexts, part of the with-me-ness research program this paper extends (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.3-4, 9-10).

target: Byrne, B., Freebody, P., & Gates, A. (1992)
note: Sharma et al.'s own finding -- that good performers/high-motivation students have greater content coverage and reading time -- directly contradicts Byrne et al.'s longitudinal finding that the best-performing readers were the fastest readers (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.15-16).

target: Reinking, D. (1988)
note: Cited alongside Byrne et al. as part of an unresolved prior literature finding no relation between comprehension and reading time, contextualizing rather than adjudicating the paper's own reading-time result (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.15-16).

target: Millis, K.K., & King, A. (2001); Dowhower, S.L. (1987)
note: The authors explicitly distinguish their AOI-backtrack construct from the literal-rereading-improves-comprehension finding in this cited literature, since students refer back to still-visible slide content rather than rereading completed material, cautioning that the parallel should be drawn only cautiously (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.16).

target: reading-time-vs-performance debate (speed-as-skill vs. coverage/dwell-time-as-engagement)
note: Surfaces the divergence between Byrne et al.'s speed-based reading-performance finding and this paper's own coverage/dwell-time-based finding, resolving it only by invoking Just and Carpenter's caution that there is no single mode of reading, without itself adjudicating between the two accounts (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.15-16).

target: content-coverage / with-me-ness mediation model (Table 2; Figs. 6, 8-10)
note: Worked example of the paper's central mediation finding: motivation predicts content coverage and with-me-ness (both perceptual and conceptual), each of which fully mediates the motivation-learning relationship, while AOI misses/backtracks only partially mediate it (FAITHFUL-Sharma et al., p.10-13, 16-17).

target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study) -- eye-tracking channel
note: ****** UNVERIFIED: Sharma et al.'s four-level gaze-variable framework (content coverage, scanpath/AOI variables, perceptual and conceptual with-me-ness) offers a plausible methodological template for a future VR attention study's eye-tracking channel, but VR headset-integrated eye tracking differs substantially in geometry (3D gaze vectors, headset-relative AOIs, no external teacher-deixis channel) from this study's 2D screen-based paradigm; linkage requires the dataset entry's own instrumentation to be confirmed (P/anticipatory-application).

target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study) -- ML/predictive-analytics channel
note: ****** UNVERIFIED: The VGG-19-heat-map-feature-extraction + LASSO + Gaussian-Process/SVM/Random-Forest/GAM regression pipeline offers a concrete engineering template for a future automated engagement/boredom-scoring layer built on VR gaze data, but this is unconfirmed until the dataset entry specifies its own instrumentation and whether it would attempt an analogous AI-prediction layer at all (P/anticipatory-application).

target: Part III self-report/behavioral-log triangulation problem
note: P/anticipatory-application -- Sharma et al.'s own framing gap (click-stream/keystream analytics fail to capture passive video watching) parallels the evidentiary gap Part III faces with self-report and behavioral-log measures of student boredom in VLE settings; their response (adding a stimulus-derived, multi-level gaze-variable framework) offers Part III a template for triangulating a self-report boredom/motivation measure against independent behavioral channels, complementary to the EEG-gaze triangulation modeled in Kim et al. (bor-sec-28).

target: Part III VLE co-watching / joint-attention correction
note: P/anticipatory-application -- the with-me-ness construct (gaze-based teacher-student co-attention, perceptual + conceptual) is a plausible proxy instrument for measuring joint/shared attention in VLE co-watching contexts; given the corrected Part III reading that the VLE's spatial-proximity-plus-voice co-watching design entails structural, group-assigned co-attention rather than an individually chosen WE, with-me-ness-style measures could in principle test whether that structurally mandated co-attention is actually achieved at the level of gaze.

target: Part III motivation-vs-boredom vocabulary boundary caution
note: P/anticipatory-application -- this source's own silence on 'boredom' (zero occurrences in the full text) is an instructive caution: a well-instrumented, nineteen-page motivation/attention study can proceed productively without ever invoking boredom as a construct, so motivation-deficit or low-engagement findings drawn from adjacent educational-technology/eye-tracking literature should not be treated as automatically equivalent to a boredom finding when Part III cites STEM sources of this kind.
